question: Should gogcli support the new public `--if-version` Drive replacement contract by retaining a narrowly scoped Drive v2 dependency for ETag-based atomic writes?
rationale: The patch is technically bounded and proven, but source tests cannot choose the repository's long-term support policy for an older Google Drive API surface or the intended user experience when that API becomes unavailable.

options.title: Accept the isolated Drive v2 path
options.body: Keep Drive v2 limited to opt-in conditional replacement, preserve unconditional Drive v3 replacement, and document that unavailable preconditions fail closed.

options.title: Require a v3-only design
options.body: Do not add the Drive v2 service boundary and request a conditional-write mechanism that remains entirely on the supported Drive v3 surface.

recommendation.title: Accept the isolated Drive v2 path
recommendation.body: Keep Drive v2 limited to opt-in conditional replacement, preserve unconditional Drive v3 replacement, and document that unavailable preconditions fail closed.

likelyOwner.reason: The current head commit integrates the affected Drive command, runtime service factory, and retry transport surfaces.
